title: "JQI_SocialClass"
output: html_document

```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}
# Setup -------------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(MASS)
library(broom)


# Load data
gss_all <- readRDS(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_job_quality_primary_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. class coding
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# class:
# 1 = Lower class
# 2 = Working class
# 3 = Middle class
# 4 = Upper class
# 5 = No class
#
# We omit "no class" because it is substantively distinct from the
# ordered class categories and is very small.

gss_all <- gss_all %>%
  mutate(
    class_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(class)),
    prestige = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(prestg10))
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Coverage of class
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

gss_all %>%
  filter(
    class_num %in% 1:4
  ) %>%
  count(year) %>%
  arrange(year)

gss_all %>%
  filter(
    class_num %in% 1:4
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n_years = n_distinct(year),
    first_year = min(year),
    last_year = max(year),
    n_obs = n()
  )

# Confirm that 2024 is not covered
gss_all %>%
  count(year, class_num) %>%
  filter(year == 2024)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Construct ordered class variable
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_class <- gss_all %>%
  mutate(
    social_class = case_when(
      class_num == 1 ~ "Lower class",
      class_num == 2 ~ "Working class",
      class_num == 3 ~ "Middle class",
      class_num == 4 ~ "Upper class",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    social_class = factor(
      social_class,
      levels = c(
        "Lower class",
        "Working class",
        "Middle class",
        "Upper class"
      ),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(social_class),
    !is.na(compensation),
    !is.na(benefits),
    !is.na(earnings_stability),
    !is.na(jqi_primary),
    !is.na(prestige)
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Analytic sample
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_class %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_years = n_distinct(year),
    first_year = min(year),
    last_year = max(year),
    n_industries = n_distinct(industry_common)
  )

jqi_class %>%
  count(social_class)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Descriptive distribution of social class
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

class_distribution <- jqi_class %>%
  count(year, social_class) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

print(class_distribution)

write_csv(
  class_distribution,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "JQI_SocialClass_YearDistribution.csv"
  )
)

# Overall distribution
jqi_class %>%
  count(social_class) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Basic race coding
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_class <- jqi_class %>%
  mutate(
    race_group = case_when(
      racecen1 == 1 ~ "White",
      racecen1 == 2 ~ "Black",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    race_group = factor(
      race_group,
      levels = c("White", "Black")
    )
  )

jqi_class_race <- jqi_class %>%
  filter(!is.na(race_group))

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Race and self-identified class
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

race_class_distribution <- jqi_class_race %>%
  count(race_group, social_class) %>%
  group_by(race_group) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

race_class_distribution

write_csv(
  race_class_distribution,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "JQI_SocialClass_RaceDistribution.csv"
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Descriptive racial difference in class
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ordered numeric version for descriptive purposes
jqi_class_race <- jqi_class_race %>%
  mutate(
    social_class_numeric = as.numeric(social_class)
  )

m_class_race_ols <- lm(
  social_class_numeric ~ race_group,
  data = jqi_class_race
)

summary(m_class_race_ols)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Model 1: Race only
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_class_race <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~ race_group,
  data = jqi_class_race,
  Hess = TRUE
)

summary(m_class_race)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Model 2: Race + occupational prestige
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_class_prestige <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~
    race_group +
    prestige,
  data = jqi_class_race,
  Hess = TRUE
)

summary(m_class_prestige)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Model 3: Race + objective employment quality
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_class_jqi <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~
    race_group +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_class_race,
  Hess = TRUE
)

summary(m_class_jqi)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Model 4: Race + prestige + objective employment quality
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_class_full <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~
    race_group +
    prestige +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_class_race,
  Hess = TRUE
)

summary(m_class_full)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Extract ordered-logit coefficients
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

class_models <- list(
  race_only = m_class_race,
  prestige = m_class_prestige,
  jqi = m_class_jqi,
  full = m_class_full
)

class_model_results <- map_dfr(
  class_models,
  ~ broom::tidy(.x),
  .id = "model"
)

print(class_model_results)

write_csv(
  class_model_results,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "JQI_SocialClass_ModelResults.csv"
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 14. Compare race coefficient across models
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
race_coefficient_comparison <- class_model_results %>%
  filter(term == "race_groupBlack") %>%
  dplyr::select(
    model,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    coef.type
  )

race_coefficient_comparison

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. OLS versions for easier coefficient comparison
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_class_ols_race <- lm(
  social_class_numeric ~ race_group,
  data = jqi_class_race
)

m_class_ols_prestige <- lm(
  social_class_numeric ~
    race_group +
    prestige,
  data = jqi_class_race
)

m_class_ols_jqi <- lm(
  social_class_numeric ~
    race_group +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_class_race
)

m_class_ols_full <- lm(
  social_class_numeric ~
    race_group +
    prestige +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_class_race
)

ols_class_models <- list(
  race_only = m_class_ols_race,
  prestige = m_class_ols_prestige,
  jqi = m_class_ols_jqi,
  full = m_class_ols_full
)

ols_class_results <- map_dfr(
  ols_class_models,
  ~ broom::tidy(.x),
  .id = "model"
)

print(ols_class_results)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. Predicted probabilities of social class by race
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Create prediction data
# Continuous predictors are held at their sample means.
# Race is varied between White and Black.

prediction_data <- jqi_class_race %>%
  summarise(
    prestige = mean(prestige, na.rm = TRUE),
    compensation = mean(compensation, na.rm = TRUE),
    benefits = mean(benefits, na.rm = TRUE),
    earnings_stability = mean(earnings_stability, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(
    race_group = factor(
      c("White", "Black"),
      levels = levels(jqi_class_race$race_group)
    )
  )


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15a. Function to generate predicted probabilities
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

get_class_predictions <- function(model, newdata, model_name) {
  
  probs <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = newdata,
    type = "probs"
  )
  
  cbind(
    newdata,
    as.data.frame(probs)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      model = model_name
    )
}


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15b. Generate predictions from all four models
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

predicted_class_probs <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  # Race-only model
  get_class_predictions(
    m_class_race,
    prediction_data %>%
      dplyr::select(race_group),
    "Race only"
  ),
  
  # Race + occupational prestige
  get_class_predictions(
    m_class_prestige,
    prediction_data %>%
      dplyr::select(
        race_group,
        prestige
      ),
    "Race + prestige"
  ),
  
  # Race + JQI dimensions
  get_class_predictions(
    m_class_jqi,
    prediction_data %>%
      dplyr::select(
        race_group,
        compensation,
        benefits,
        earnings_stability
      ),
    "Race + JQI"
  ),
  
  # Full model
  get_class_predictions(
    m_class_full,
    prediction_data %>%
      dplyr::select(
        race_group,
        prestige,
        compensation,
        benefits,
        earnings_stability
      ),
    "Full model"
  )
)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15c. Inspect the predicted probabilities
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

predicted_class_probs


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15d. Reshape predicted probabilities to long format
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Get the names of the probability columns returned by polr
probability_columns <- colnames(
  predict(
    m_class_race,
    newdata = prediction_data %>%
      dplyr::select(race_group),
    type = "probs"
  )
)

probability_columns


predicted_class_probs_long <- predicted_class_probs %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(probability_columns),
    names_to = "social_class",
    values_to = "probability"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    social_class = factor(
      social_class,
      levels = probability_columns
    ),
    race = factor(
      race_group,
      levels = c("White", "Black")
    )
  )


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15e. Create a compact predicted-probability table
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

predicted_class_table <- predicted_class_probs_long %>%
  mutate(
    probability = round(probability, 3)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    model,
    race,
    social_class,
    probability
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    model,
    race,
    social_class
  )

predicted_class_table


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15f. Calculate Black–White differences in predicted probabilities
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

predicted_class_gaps <- predicted_class_probs_long %>%
  dplyr::select(
    model,
    race,
    social_class,
    probability
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = race,
    values_from = probability
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    black_white_difference = Black - White
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    model,
    social_class
  )

predicted_class_gaps


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15g. Plot predicted probabilities
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

class_probability_plot <- ggplot(
  predicted_class_probs_long,
  aes(
    x = race,
    y = probability
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    social_class ~ model
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Predicted probability",
    title = "Predicted Social-Class Identification by Race",
    subtitle = "Predictions hold occupational prestige and job-quality dimensions at their sample means"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

class_probability_plot


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15h. Save figure
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  here::here(
    "04_figures",
    "SocialClass_PredictedProbabilities_Race.png"
  ),
  class_probability_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 9,
  dpi = 300
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 16. Add real income as a control
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Inspect realrinc first
summary(jqi_class_race$realrinc)

# Check the distribution and missing-value codes
table(
  jqi_class_race$realrinc,
  useNA = "ifany"
)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 16a. Create log real income
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_class_race <- jqi_class_race %>%
  mutate(
    realrinc_clean = case_when(
      is.na(realrinc) ~ NA_real_,
      realrinc < 0 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(realrinc)
    ),
    log_realrinc = log1p(realrinc_clean)
  )


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 16b. Create complete-case dataset for income models
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_class_income <- jqi_class_race %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(social_class),
    !is.na(race_group),
    !is.na(log_realrinc)
  )


# Check sample size
nrow(jqi_class_income)

# Check income distribution
summary(jqi_class_income$log_realrinc)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 16c. Ordered-logit models
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Model 1: Race only
m_class_race_income <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~ race_group + log_realrinc,
  data = jqi_class_income,
  Hess = TRUE
)


# Model 2: Race + income + prestige
m_class_prestige_income <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~ race_group +
    log_realrinc +
    prestige,
  data = jqi_class_income,
  Hess = TRUE
)


# Model 3: Race + income + JQI
m_class_jqi_income <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~ race_group +
    log_realrinc +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_class_income,
  Hess = TRUE
)


# Model 4: Full model
m_class_full_income <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~ race_group +
    log_realrinc +
    prestige +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_class_income,
  Hess = TRUE
)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 16d. Model summaries
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

summary(m_class_race_income)

summary(m_class_prestige_income)

summary(m_class_jqi_income)

summary(m_class_full_income)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 16e. Compare the race coefficients
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

race_income_comparison <- tibble::tibble(
  model = c(
    "Race + income",
    "Race + income + prestige",
    "Race + income + JQI",
    "Full model"
  ),
  estimate = c(
    coef(m_class_race_income)["race_groupBlack"],
    coef(m_class_prestige_income)["race_groupBlack"],
    coef(m_class_jqi_income)["race_groupBlack"],
    coef(m_class_full_income)["race_groupBlack"]
  ),
  std.error = c(
    sqrt(diag(vcov(m_class_race_income)))["race_groupBlack"],
    sqrt(diag(vcov(m_class_prestige_income)))["race_groupBlack"],
    sqrt(diag(vcov(m_class_jqi_income)))["race_groupBlack"],
    sqrt(diag(vcov(m_class_full_income)))["race_groupBlack"]
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    statistic = estimate / std.error
  )

race_income_comparison


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 16f. Calculate attenuation relative to the race-only model
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

baseline_race_beta <- coef(m_class_race)["race_groupBlack"]

race_income_comparison <- race_income_comparison %>%
  mutate(
    attenuation_percent =
      100 * (abs(baseline_race_beta) - abs(estimate)) /
      abs(baseline_race_beta)
  )

race_income_comparison

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 17. Predicted probabilities with income control
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

prediction_data_income <- jqi_class_income %>%
  summarise(
    log_realrinc = mean(log_realrinc, na.rm = TRUE),
    prestige = mean(prestige, na.rm = TRUE),
    compensation = mean(compensation, na.rm = TRUE),
    benefits = mean(benefits, na.rm = TRUE),
    earnings_stability = mean(earnings_stability, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(
    race_group = factor(
      c("White", "Black"),
      levels = levels(jqi_class_income$race_group)
    )
  )


# Function to generate predicted probabilities

get_class_predictions_income <- function(

    newdata,

) {
  
  probs <- predict(

    newdata = newdata,
    type = "probs"
  )
  
  cbind(
    newdata,
    as.data.frame(probs)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      model = model_name
    )
}


# Generate predictions

predicted_class_probs_income <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  
  get_class_predictions_income(

    prediction_data_income %>%
      dplyr::select(
        race_group,
        log_realrinc

      dplyr::select(
        race_group,
        log_realrinc,
        prestige
      ),

  ),
  
  get_class_predictions_income(
    m_class_jqi_income,

      dplyr::select(
        race_group,
        log_realrinc,
        compensation,
        benefits,
        earnings_stability
      ),
    "Race + income + JQI"
  ),
  
  get_class_predictions_income(
    m_class_full_income,
    prediction_data_income %>%
      dplyr::select(
        race_group,
        log_realrinc,
        prestige,
        compensation,
        benefits,
        earnings_stability
      ),
    "Full model"
  )
)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 17a. Reshape predicted probabilities

probability_columns_income <- colnames(
  predict(
    m_class_race_income,
    newdata = prediction_data_income %>%
      dplyr::select(
        race_group,
        log_realrinc
      ),
    type = "probs"
  )
)


predicted_class_probs_income_long <- predicted_class_probs_income %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

predicted_class_gaps_income <- predicted_class_probs_income_long %>%
  dplyr::select(

  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(

predicted_class_gaps_income


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

class_probability_income_plot <- ggplot(

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 16. Calculate attenuation of the Black coefficient
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
race_beta <- ols_class_results %>%
  filter(term == "race_groupBlack") %>%
  dplyr::select(model, estimate)



race_beta

race_only_beta <- race_beta %>%
  filter(model == "race_only") %>%
  pull(estimate)

race_prestige_beta <- race_beta %>%
  filter(model == "prestige") %>%
  pull(estimate)

race_jqi_beta <- race_beta %>%
  filter(model == "jqi") %>%
  pull(estimate)

race_full_beta <- race_beta %>%
  filter(model == "full") %>%
  pull(estimate)

attenuation_results <- tibble(
  comparison = c(
    "Prestige relative to race-only",
    "JQI relative to race-only",
    "Prestige + JQI relative to race-only"
  ),
  race_coefficient = c(
    race_prestige_beta,
    race_jqi_beta,
    race_full_beta
  ),
  percent_attenuation = c(
    1 - abs(race_prestige_beta / race_only_beta),
    1 - abs(race_jqi_beta / race_only_beta),
    1 - abs(race_full_beta / race_only_beta)
  )
)

attenuation_results

write_csv(
  attenuation_results,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "JQI_SocialClass_RaceCoefficientAttenuation.csv"
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 17. Do JQI dimensions interact with race?
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_class_jqi_race_interactions <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~
    race_group * compensation +
    race_group * benefits +
    race_group * earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_class_race,
  Hess = TRUE
)

summary(m_class_jqi_race_interactions)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 18. Joint test of racial moderation
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_class_jqi_race_restricted <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~
    race_group +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_class_race,
  Hess = TRUE
)

# Likelihood-ratio test
anova(
  m_class_jqi_race_restricted,
  m_class_jqi_race_interactions,
  test = "Chisq"
)

year_race_class_distribution <- jqi_class_race %>%
  count(year, race_group, social_class) %>%
  group_by(year, race_group) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  ) %>%

year_race_class_distribution

write_csv(

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 20. Year-specific JQI → class models
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

year_class_models <- jqi_class_race %>%
  group_split(year) %>%
  map_dfr(
    ~ {
      yr <- unique(.x$year)

      model <- MASS::polr(
        social_class ~
          race_group +
          compensation +
          benefits +
          earnings_stability,
        data = .x,
        Hess = TRUE
      )

      tidy(model) %>%
        mutate(year = yr)
    }
  )

year_class_models

write_csv(
  year_class_models,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "JQI_SocialClass_YearModels.csv"
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 18. Year-specific ordered-logit models controlling for income
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Make sure the income-controlled analysis dataset contains all variables
# needed for the models.

jqi_class_income <- jqi_class_race %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(social_class),
    !is.na(race_group),
    !is.na(log_realrinc),
    !is.na(compensation),
    !is.na(benefits),
    !is.na(earnings_stability),
    !is.na(prestige)
  )


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 18a. Estimate year-specific models
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

class_years <- sort(unique(jqi_class_income$year))


year_class_models_income <- purrr::map_dfr(
  
  class_years,
  
  function(y) {
    
    year_data <- jqi_class_income %>%
      filter(year == y)
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Model 1: Race + income + JQI
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    
    m_jqi <- MASS::polr(
      social_class ~
        race_group +
        log_realrinc +
        compensation +
        benefits +
        earnings_stability,
      data = year_data,
      Hess = TRUE
    )
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Model 2: Race + income + prestige + JQI
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    
    m_full <- MASS::polr(
      social_class ~
        race_group +
        log_realrinc +
        prestige +
        compensation +
        benefits +
        earnings_stability,
      data = year_data,
      Hess = TRUE
    )
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Extract coefficient results
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    
    tidy_jqi <- broom::tidy(m_jqi) %>%
      mutate(
        year = y,
        model = "Income + JQI"
      )
    
    tidy_full <- broom::tidy(m_full) %>%
      mutate(
        year = y,
        model = "Income + prestige + JQI"
      )
    
    bind_rows(
      tidy_jqi,
      tidy_full
    )
  }
)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 18b. Examine the racial coefficients
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

year_race_income_results <- year_class_models_income %>%
  filter(
    term == "race_groupBlack"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    model,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    model,
    year
  )

year_race_income_results


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 18c. Compare race coefficients across the two specifications
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

year_race_income_comparison <- year_race_income_results %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = model,
    values_from = c(
      estimate,
      std.error,
      statistic
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(year)

year_race_income_comparison


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 18d. Calculate attenuation from adding prestige
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

year_race_income_comparison <- year_race_income_comparison %>%
  mutate(
    prestige_attenuation_percent =
      100 * (
        abs(`estimate_Income + JQI`) -
        abs(`estimate_Income + prestige + JQI`)
      ) /
      abs(`estimate_Income + JQI`)
  )

year_race_income_comparison


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 18e. Extract the JQI coefficients by year
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

year_jqi_income_results <- year_class_models_income %>%
  filter(
    term %in% c(
      "compensation",
      "benefits",
      "earnings_stability",
      "log_realrinc",
      "prestige"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    model,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    model,
    year,
    term
  )

year_jqi_income_results


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 18f. Create a plot of the income-controlled racial coefficients
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

year_race_income_plot <- ggplot(
  year_race_income_results,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = estimate,
    group = model,
    linetype = model
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = class_years
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Black coefficient",
    linetype = "Model",
    title = "The Racial Difference in Self-Identified Class Persists After Controlling for Income",
    subtitle = "Year-specific ordered-logit models"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

year_race_income_plot


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 18g. Save plot
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  here::here(
    "04_figures",
    "SocialClass_RaceCoefficient_IncomeControlled_OverTime.png"
  ),
  year_race_income_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 19. Formal tests of temporal heterogeneity in the racial class difference
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# These tests ask whether the Black–White difference in self-identified
# social class changes systematically across survey years.
#
# The restricted model assumes that the racial difference is constant
# across years, while allowing the overall distribution of social class
# to vary by year.
#
# The unrestricted model allows the Black–White difference to vary by year
# through the race_group × year interaction.
#
# We use likelihood-ratio tests to determine whether allowing the racial
# coefficient to vary across years significantly improves model fit.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 19a. Income + JQI specification
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Restricted model:
# Common Black–White difference across years
# Year fixed effects capture changes in the overall distribution of
# self-identified social class.

m_class_income_jqi_common <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~
    race_group +
    log_realrinc +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability +
    factor(year),
  data = jqi_class_income,
  Hess = TRUE
)


# Unrestricted model:
# Allows the Black–White difference to vary across years.

m_class_income_jqi_race_year <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~
    race_group * factor(year) +
    log_realrinc +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_class_income,
  Hess = TRUE
)


# Formal likelihood-ratio test
# H0: The Black–White difference is constant across years.
# H1: The Black–White difference varies across years.

anova(
  m_class_income_jqi_common,
  m_class_income_jqi_race_year
)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 19b. Income + prestige + JQI specification
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Restricted model:
# Common Black–White difference across years.

m_class_income_full_common <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~
    race_group +
    log_realrinc +
    prestige +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability +
    factor(year),
  data = jqi_class_income,
  Hess = TRUE
)


# Unrestricted model:
# Allows the Black–White difference to vary across years.

m_class_income_full_race_year <- MASS::polr(
  social_class ~
    race_group * factor(year) +
    log_realrinc +
    prestige +
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_class_income,
  Hess = TRUE
)


# Formal likelihood-ratio test
# H0: The Black–White difference is constant across years.
# H1: The Black–White difference varies across years.

anova(
  m_class_income_full_common,
  m_class_income_full_race_year
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

Objective employment quality: Adding compensation, benefits, and earnings stability also barely changes it.Occupational prestige: Adding prestige produces a modest attenuation, but a substantial racial difference remains. And this pattern is persistent over time.

sessionInfo()
```
